A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, On the Importance of Gaussianizing Representations. All 20 pages, including Appendices A–F, equations, four tables, and thirteen figures, are available and readable.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural-network training experiments, normalization comparisons, ablations, and appendix results on noise robustness, runtime, and feature distributions.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendices A and E.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same power transform, single Newton–Raphson estimation step, scaled additive Gaussian noise, and inference procedure. Section 5.7 corrects the estimator's description without changing its computation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same image-classification coverage: CIFAR10, CIFAR100, STL10, SVHN, Caltech101, TinyImageNet, Food101, and ImageNet. The noise-perturbation scenarios and other experimental coverage are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain BatchNorm, LayerNorm, InstanceNorm, GroupNorm, decorrelated BatchNorm, Gaussian dropout, and unscaled additive Gaussian noise. Figure 11's correction from BatchNormal to BatchNorm identifies the existing comparator rather than introducing another method.

E3.justification: The training budgets, architectures, augmentations, splits, metrics, minibatch settings, and noise-evaluation procedures remain unchanged in Section 5 and Appendices A and F. Equation 6 and its gaussianization-strength experiment are unchanged despite revised estimator terminology.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same component ablations, gaussianization-strength sweep, width/depth/minibatch analyses, noise-robustness tests, normality and independence analyses, and approximation checks. No analytical question or supporting experiment is added or removed.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 retains six independently initialized models, numerical reporting with one standard error, and graphical 95% confidence intervals where applicable. Table 4 retains six Monte Carlo noise draws, and Appendix F retains the same split-seed disclosure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical entries, and all embedded plots are identical. For example, Table 1 reports the same ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 71.54 ± 0.16 for LN and 75.25 ± 0.07 for LNN. No experimental findings are added or removed.

T1.justification: Theorem 2.1, Lemma B.1, the noise-robustness definition, and the derivations in Appendices C–D are unchanged. The added prose about moment constraints restates assumptions already present in v1's theorem; the estimator terminology correction changes no mathematical definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about gaussianizing representations, generalization, applicability across normalization layers, and noise robustness without additional learnable parameters.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 explicitly connects moment constraints to conventional normalization and removes 'direct' from the MSE-proxy description. Section 5.7 replaces the misleading MLE characterization with Newton–Raphson solution. Appendix A.2 explicitly acknowledges runtime increases instead of emphasizing similar test-time performance, aligning it with the existing main-text summary.

D1.justification: Implementation and training details, hyperparameters, V100 timing hardware, and the code-availability statement are unchanged. Appendix F merely expands the acronym MLP; the new acknowledgments add no technical reproduction instructions.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Deep Neural Networks as Gaussian Processes is updated from its 2017 arXiv entry to its 2018 ICLR publication, with corresponding citation metadata corrections; this is the same work.

P1.justification: v2 adds acknowledgments, revises the impact-statement wording, corrects estimator terminology, and makes localized prose and bibliographic edits. The section sequence, overall narrative, and most text remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 11's caption corrects BatchNormal to BatchNorm and receives minor wording edits. The added footnote and acknowledgments cause limited layout reflow. Figure graphics and table structures remain unchanged, with no displays added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 improves technical precision by correctly identifying the Newton–Raphson estimate in Section 5.7 and clarifying the constrained motivation in Section 2.1. Appendix A.2 also describes runtime overhead more consistently. These resolve localized ambiguities while leaving the method, formal results, and empirical evidence unchanged.
